# ConnectorZone

> A free catalog of Model Context Protocol connectors with copy ready configuration for nine
> MCP capable clients. Built from the official MCP Registry, 19,630 records read
> on 2026-08-02, 14,240 profiles published.

ConnectorZone is an independent aggregator. It is not affiliated with Anthropic, OpenAI,
Google, Microsoft, GitHub, Anysphere or the Model Context Protocol project. A registry listing
is a namespace ownership check, not a security review, and this site does not execute or audit
connectors.

## What this site adds over the registry

- Registry package metadata resolved into a runnable command per package type.
- The exact configuration block each client expects, across four different config shapes.
- A compatibility verdict per client with the rule and the documentation date behind it.
- A completeness score with a published breakdown, and gates that keep thin records out.

## Core pages

- [Connector directory](https://connector.zone/connectors/): 14,240 profiles, filterable by transport, credential and client.
- [Client reference](https://connector.zone/clients/): where each client keeps configuration and which transports it documents.
- [Categories](https://connector.zone/categories/): 21 derived categories.
- [Collections](https://connector.zone/collections/): curated sets selected by published rules.
- [Methodology](https://connector.zone/methodology/): scoring, gating and compatibility rules in full.
- [Data status](https://connector.zone/status/): the exact registry snapshot behind this build.
- [Data endpoints](https://connector.zone/api/): static JSON for the catalog.

## Guides

- [How to choose an MCP connector](https://connector.zone/guides/choosing-a-connector/): A practical filter for picking connectors that will still work in six months, based on what the registry actually tells you.
- [A security review for MCP connectors](https://connector.zone/guides/mcp-security/): What a registry listing does and does not tell you, and the review that actually reduces risk before you attach a connector.
- [Local servers or hosted endpoints](https://connector.zone/guides/local-vs-remote/): The trade between running a connector on your machine and attaching one over HTTPS, and how to tell which your situation calls for.
- [OAuth and authorisation in MCP](https://connector.zone/guides/oauth-and-authorization/): How authorisation works for HTTP based MCP servers, what the consent screen is really telling you, and where keys still make sense.
- [Configuring MCP in every major client](https://connector.zone/guides/client-configuration/): Where each client keeps its config, which key name it expects and the specific mistakes that stop a server loading.
- [What the 2026-07-28 protocol revision changes](https://connector.zone/guides/protocol-2026-07-28/): The current specification revision, what moved since the previous one, and how to tell whether your client and servers are aligned.
- [Debugging a connector that will not load](https://connector.zone/guides/debugging-connections/): An ordered checklist for the silent failures, from invalid JSON to tool budgets, with the command that answers each one.
- [Reading provenance in the MCP registry](https://connector.zone/guides/connector-provenance/): What a namespace proves, how to spot bulk publishing, and why the catalog caps how many entries one publisher can contribute.

Connector records come from the official Model Context Protocol Registry under CC0 1.0.
Original ConnectorZone text, scoring rules and category definitions are the work of this
project. Attribution with a link is appreciated when reusing either.
